# Solver sources and browser adaptation

- UR ur_kinematics: https://github.com/ros-industrial/universal_robot
  Revision: 39ad110d8f2e8f66856a201cca88aa7a7025e3eb (noetic-devel).
  ur/ur_kin.cpp and ur/ur_kin.h are retained upstream source. ur/ur-kinematics.js is a JavaScript syntax port of the upstream forward/inverse functions with UR5 constants, generated by scripts/build-solvers.mjs. BSD copyright and full license retained.
- closed-chain-ik-js: https://github.com/gkjohnson/closed-chain-ik-js
  Revision: 35e50d6551772762c2f79eefd8a3221adcd1fb53.
  closed-chain-ik.js bundles the unmodified upstream core with dependencies. Apache-2.0 license retained in CLOSED-CHAIN-LICENSE. No network download required at runtime.
- Dependencies: gl-matrix 3.4.4 (MIT), linear-solve 1.2.1 (MIT, upstream package/README declarations retained), svd-js 1.1.1 (MIT). Available license notices are included alongside the bundle.

App integration: dist/solvers.js. UR target frames transform between scene TCP, tool offset and the repository end-effector convention. Up to eight UR solutions normalize to the current angles; the nearest valid solution is chosen. The iterative solver constructs the actual URDF chain and seeds from the current pose; unresolved goals stop without falling back to another algorithm.

The current solver remains the original fixed-downward analytic solver. Repository solvers hold current TCP orientation during position control. Smooth motion, joint limits (-360 to 360 degrees), collision checks and held payload transforms remain application behavior. Direct joint controls bypass inverse kinematics, run bounded forward-kinematic movement and stop on collisions. Returning to the current solver gradually restores the downward pose; the other solvers preserve orientation.

Validation: node tests/solvers.test.mjs; existing motion/horizontal-motion/grippers/collision/items tests. This is a browser kinematic simulation, not a physical robot controller.
